name: 14 Uncensored AI Providers
title: 14 Uncensored AI Providers
lead: With the Compare your local AI kit, you give the same fictional meeting minutes to two models and check their answers, response times, and memory use.
summary: This kit helps anyone choosing an AI to run on their own computer. You give the models fictional meeting minutes and check whether they get the maintenance date right and recognize that the minutes omit the name of the person who approved it. The comparison brings together 14 variants of local models and points to the standard versions. To repeat the exercise, have a local model already downloaded.
models_lead: Barty Bart reports 725 results for standard and modified versions. This table lists the models and file sizes used in the comparison. The links open standard versions. In the last row, Qwen 3.5 9B is an official alternative of a similar size. The standard version of Qwen 3.8 9B has no direct link.
only_modified: Only the modified version was tested
kit_heading: Compare using the same meeting minutes
kit_steps: Open a model you have already downloaded and disconnect from the network. Start a blank conversation with external tools turned off.
Paste the same prompt into each model. Time from submission until the response is complete. If possible, note the memory use right afterward, while the model is still open.
Compare with the answer key. Mark whether the date is correct, the name is omitted, and the response is in Portuguese. If the model fails to load, leave the quality field blank.
proof_lead: In the INEMA run, Llama 3.2 took 3.37 s with the network isolated. The software reported 2.3 GB allocated to the model after the response. The AI got the date right and said the team approved it, but only implied that the minutes did not include a name.
table_note: File size and memory use are different measurements. Memory use varies with the software, text length, and machine configuration.
pt_files: The exercise files are in Portuguese.
memory_help: On Windows, open Task Manager and go to Performance → GPU. If the AI is using the graphics card, copy the value currently in use before the capacity bar, using the same metric in both runs. If there is no comparable reading, leave the memory field blank.
